segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
a silver brazier of lanterns,
whose weight was forty liters according to the Syrian liter,
that is, each liter being six liters according to the Baghdadi [standard],
along with other vessels and many ornaments.
And the first king from the Franks reigned in it in the year 1410 [of the Greeks = 1099 AD],
for two years.
And after him, Baldwin {OCR?} for seventeen years.
And when the Egyptians heard of what had happened in Egypt [read: Palestine / Jerusalem?],
al-Afdal, the son of the commander of the army, set out with a large force.
And the Franks came
and encountered them near Ascalon,
and the Arabs [Muslims] were defeated.
And the Franks killed a great number of them,
and the rest fled and entered Ascalon.
And when the people of Ascalon gave them twelve thousand dinars,
they left them and returned to Jerusalem.
And in the year 492
of the Arabs [1099 AD]:
the Turkish chieftains rebelled against Sultan Barkyaruq,
on account of the vizier Majd al-Dawlah, who was treating them badly;
and they killed the vizier,
and deserted Barkyaruq,
and went to his brother Muhammad,
and made him king over them.
And he was also accepted by the Caliph,
and a diploma was written for him,
and he was proclaimed: Ghiyath al-Dunya wa'l-Din Abu Shuja' Muhammad, the Sultan.
And Barkyaruq fled to Baghdad,
and Sultan Muhammad pursued after him.
And many times they clashed with one another,
and they were routing and being routed.
At this time, that is, in the year 493
of the Arabs [1100 AD]:
Yahya, the physician of Baghdad, the son of Jazlah, died.
He was the author of the famous book *Minhaj*, which is in the hands of the physicians of our time,
concerning simple and compound medicines and diets.
This man was a Christian,
and from a certain Arab [Muslim] logician,
whose name was Abu Ali ibn al-Walid,
he was learning logic.
And when he sophistically argued to him
that not even the loving and personal union,
of which the Nestorians speak,
can be reasonably conceived concerning the divine nature,
he deceived him, and he converted to Islam.
It is said
that he was wealthy,
and to his friends... {OCR?}

Baldwin,
Baudouin.
